counterexample: S = {x in R : x <= 1} (A = [1], b = 1, so b_1 > 0). True polar: y*x <= 1 for all x <= 1 forces y >= 0 (let x -> -infinity) and y <= 1 (at x = 1), so S° = [0,1]. The formula asserted at line 0047 gives {y : y*a_1 <= b_1} = {y : y <= 1} = (-infinity, 1], which is not even bounded below and hence not equal to S°. Also, the per-row reduction of line 0031 is false here in the multi-row case: for S = {x in R^2 : x_1 <= 1, x_2 <= 1} the claimed conditions y_1 <= 1, y_2 <= 1 omit y >= 0. Separately, the biconditional of lines 0015-0020 fails when S is empty: take m = 1, A = 0 (the 1 x n zero row), b = -1; then S = empty and S° = R^n, but A^T lambda = 0 for every lambda, so no lambda >= 0 represents y != 0.
reasoning_summary: 0001-0003 Statement of what is to be proved; no mathematical content, fine. 0004-0005 Standard definition of polyhedron as a finite intersection of half-spaces, equivalently {x : Ax <= b}; correct. 0006-0007 Standard definition of the polar set, matching the problem; correct. 0008 Header, no content. 0009-0011 Legitimate use of the hypothesis: S polyhedron gives A, b with S = {x : Ax <= b}; fine. 0012-0013 Direct restatement of the definition of S° for this S; correct. 0014-0020 Invokes affine Farkas / LP duality: y^T x <= 1 on {x : Ax <= b} iff exists lambda >= 0 with A^T lambda = y and b^T lambda <= 1. The (<=) direction is immediate (y^T x = lambda^T A x <= lambda^T b <= 1). The (=>) direction is the standard duality result but holds only when S is nonempty; the proof never assumes or checks feasibility, and the equivalence is false for infeasible systems (A = 0, b = -1 gives S° = R^n but only y = 0 is representable). Gap, though not fatal since the empty case still yields the polyhedron R^n. 0021-0022 Faithful restatement of the previous characterization; follows from 0014-0020. 0023-0024 Correct: {(y, lambda) : A^T lambda = y, b^T lambda <= 1, lambda >= 0} is defined by finitely many linear equalities/inequalities in R^{n+m}, hence a polyhedron, and S° is its image under the projection (y, lambda) -> y. 0025-0026 Correct appeal to the fact that coordinate projections of polyhedra are polyhedra (Fourier-Motzkin); the main argument is complete here, modulo the empty-S caveat above. 0027-0032 FIRST OUTRIGHT FAILURE: it claims that membership y in S° forces y^T x <= 1 for every x satisfying the single inequality a_i^T x <= b_i. This is false; S° only constrains y against points of S = intersection over all i of the half-spaces, and each individual half-space is strictly larger than S, so the per-row condition is strictly stronger than (and not implied by) membership in S°. The whole 'alternative' derivation rests on this illegitimate decoupling. 0033-0040 False: sup{y^T x : a_i^T x <= b_i} is +infinity unless y is a nonnegative multiple of a_i, so the asserted maximum y^T a_i / b_i is wrong; moreover the proposed maximizer x = a_i / b_i need not even be feasible (a_i^T a_i / b_i <= b_i requires ||a_i||^2 <= b_i^2). The algebraic step from y^T a_i / b_i <= 1 to y^T a_i <= b_i is valid for b_i > 0 but is drawn from a false premise. 0041-0045 Mixed but unjustified: the isolated fact that {y : y^T x <= 0 for all x with a_i^T x <= 0} = {lambda a_i : lambda >= 0} is correct (polar of a homogeneous half-space), but it is applied per row under the invalid decoupling of 0031, and calling this set 'the recession cone of S' is a misnomer (it is the polar of a half-space, not a recession cone); the requirement y^T x <= 1 on S does not force y^T x <= 0 in this way. 0046-0047 False characterization of S°: as computed in the counterexample, S = {x <= 1} in R has S° = [0,1] while the formula yields (-infinity, 1]; furthermore, if two or more rows have b_i = 0 with non-parallel a_i, the second set collapses to {0}, again contradicting the true polar. 0048-0049 Mischaracterizes the ray {lambda a_i : lambda >= 0} as a 'line'; the inference 'finite intersection of half-spaces / polyhedra is a polyhedron' would be sound in itself, but it is applied to a set that is not S°, so the conclusion is not established by this route. 0050-0053 The final assertion 'S° is a polyhedron' is a true statement and is genuinely supported by lines 0009-0026 (for nonempty S), but the claim that it was also shown 'by explicitly constructing its half-space representation' is unsupported, since that construction (0027-0049) is incorrect. 0054 Page number, no content. Overall: the projection/duality argument is essentially right (with an unaddressed empty-polyhedron edge case at 0015-0020), but the second, explicitly asserted derivation contains false steps beginning at 0031, so per step-by-step verification the proof as written is INVALID.
